Anya: Quick question — for plan-aware routing we need per-plan fallback chains + a 'soft debit' mode where we don't immediately block but apply a grace window. Should this live in the central policy catalog or as a per-tenant override API? Also want clear telemetry tags at the point of routing.

Kevin: my 2c: keep canonical policy in the catalog (global defaults) and expose tenant overrides separately. Runtime resolves: global -> org override -> per-route override. Example policy snippet:
```json
{
  "plan": "free",
  "routes": [
    { "variant": "opt-6b", "priority": 100 },
    { "variant": "opt-2b-quant", "priority": 80, "fallback_reason": "cost" }
  ],
  "soft_debit": {
    "mode": "grace",           // "grace" | "throttle"
    "grace_window_ms": 5000,
    "soft_threshold_pct": 0.9
  },
  "quota_debit_mode": "optimistic" // optimistic vs confirmed
}
```
This gives console a single source of truth while allowing per-tenant overrides via API.

Maya: we need explicit telemetry fields. At a minimum: `routing.plan`, `routing.variant`, `routing.fallback_chain` (array), `quota.action` (allowed|soft-debit|blocked), `quota.delta_tokens`, and `region.affinity`. Dashboards should be able to pivot by plan+region+variant.

Dave: important: optimistic debit can race and let concurrent requests overspend a tenant's quota. We should implement a short-lived reservation step on the quota service: check-and-reserve with TTL and rollback on failure. Pseudo: 
```py
# reserve n tokens for tenant
if quota.reserve(tenant, n, ttl=200ms):
  proceed()
else:
  if policy.soft_debit.mode == 'grace': route_to_soft_variant()
  else: reject()
```
This avoids overdraw under high-concurrency. Also consider a background reaper to reclaim expired reservations.

Lex: UX notes: console needs a clear toggle per-plan: "Soft debit enabled" + preview of expected cost/latency impact. For rollouts, add per-org targeting + sample percent (canary). Also show a visualization of the fallback chain probabilities and estimate of SLO impact. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Anya: agree. Also region-awareness: prefer local-region variants for lower latency; allow cross-region fallback only for enterprise (opt-in) — don't want free tenants unexpectedly routed cross-region. That should be a flag in the policy: `allow_cross_region_fallback`.

Kevin: implementation detail for telemetry and tracing: runtime should emit `routing.policy.version`, `routing.chosen_variant`, `routing.fallback_reason` and `routing.chain` as tags. For sampling, we keep full chain for 1% of requests and aggregated counters for all. Telemetry payload example: `routing.chain=[opt-6b,opt-2b-quant] fallback_reason=regional_unavailable quota_action=soft-debit`.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: routing-policy-service v2.7.1 deployed to staging at 1761234600, integration tests passed, baseline fallback-rate=0.8% (staging).

Maya: can we add panels: "fallback rate by plan" (time series), "soft-debit consumed tokens by plan", and "cross-region fallbacks"? For alerts: threshold fallback_rate>5% for free or pro should create ticket.

Dave: also consider a backstop: when reservations show >10% expired (failures to confirm), temporarily degrade optimistic mode to confirmed mode for that tenant until they heal.

Lex: for rollout UX, include an "impact preview" that runs a small historical simulation on a tenant's recent traffic to estimate fallback counts and cost delta before applying changes. That will reduce surprises.

Anya: ok will draft RFC with: 1) policy schema (catalog + override), 2) quota reservation semantics, 3) telemetry tags + sampling, 4) console UX and canary flow, 5) region-affinity rules. I'll open PR and link here. :memo:

Kevin: thumbs up. If anyone wants to help review the quota reservation code I can drop a branch. @Dave?

Dave: I'll take the reservation impl + tests.

Maya: I'll sketch the dashboards and the console toggles.

Lex: I'll wire the rollout ui and the cost preview.

Anya: thanks all — assigning owners and will ping when RFC PR is up. :handshake:
